name: Romanian Deadlift (RDL)
instructions: Stand tall holding a barbell at hip height with a shoulder-width overhand grip, feet hip-width apart and knees softly unlocked.
Brace your core and pull your shoulder blades down and back to set a neutral spine.
Push your hips straight back and let the bar travel down close to your thighs, keeping a slight, fixed knee bend.
Lower until you feel a strong stretch in the hamstrings (usually mid-shin to just below the knees) without rounding your lower back.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to return to standing, finishing tall without leaning back.
formCues: Lead with the hips, not the knees — it's a hinge, not a squat.
Keep the bar dragging close to your legs the whole way.
Maintain a flat, neutral spine and a proud chest.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back at the bottom.
Turning it into a squat by bending the knees too much.
Letting the bar drift away from the body.

name: Lying Leg Curl
instructions: Lie face down on the machine and set the ankle pad just above the back of your heels, against the lower calf.
Align your knees with the machine's pivot point and grip the handles to keep your torso stable.
Curl your heels toward your glutes by contracting the hamstrings, keeping your hips pressed into the pad.
Squeeze hard at the top without letting your hips lift off the bench.
Lower under control back to the start with a slight stretch, avoiding a sudden drop.
formCues: Keep hips and pelvis pinned to the pad.
Control the negative — don't let the weight crash down.
Pause and squeeze at peak contraction.
commonMistakes: Lifting the hips to cheat the weight up.
Using momentum instead of muscular control.
Setting the ankle pad too high on the calf.

name: Seated Leg Curl
instructions: Adjust the seat so your knees line up with the machine's pivot and the back pad supports your spine.
Place the lower-leg pad just above your heels and secure the thigh pad snugly over your quads.
Grip the handles and brace, then curl your heels down and back underneath the seat.
Drive to full knee flexion and squeeze your hamstrings hard.
Return slowly to the starting position, controlling the stretch without letting the knees snap straight.
formCues: Keep the thigh pad tight so your legs don't lift.
Drive through the heels, not the toes.
Emphasize a slow, controlled negative.
commonMistakes: Bouncing out of the bottom with momentum.
Pointing the toes hard and cramping the calves.
Partial range — not curling all the way down.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
instructions: Sit on the floor with your shoulder blades resting against a bench and a padded barbell over your hips.
Plant your feet flat about hip-width apart, positioned so your shins will be vertical at the top of the movement.
Brace your core, tuck your chin slightly, and drive through your heels to extend your hips upward.
Push until your torso and thighs form a straight line, squeezing your glutes hard at the top.
Lower your hips under control back toward the floor and repeat without bouncing the bar off the ground.
formCues: Finish with a full glute squeeze and a flat back — don't overarch the lower back.
Keep your chin tucked and ribs down to stay neutral.
Drive through the heels, shins vertical at lockout.
commonMistakes: Hyperextending the lower back instead of finishing with the glutes.
Placing feet too far forward, shifting load to the hamstrings.
Cutting the range short and not reaching full hip extension.

name: Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor about hip-width apart and close to your glutes.
Rest your arms at your sides and press your lower back gently into the floor to brace.
Drive through your heels and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes firmly at the top for a brief pause.
Lower your hips under control back to the floor and repeat.
formCues: Squeeze the glutes to lift, not the lower back.
Keep ribs down and avoid arching at the top.
Drive through the heels, not the toes.
commonMistakes: Overarching the lumbar spine instead of extending the hips.
Placing feet too far away, recruiting hamstrings over glutes.
Rushing reps without a top-end squeeze.

name: Barbell Good Morning
instructions: Set a barbell across your upper traps as in a back squat, feet shoulder-width apart with knees softly bent.
Brace your core hard and set a neutral, flat spine before moving.
Hinge at the hips, pushing your glutes back as your torso tips forward toward parallel with the floor.
Lower only as far as you can keep a flat back and feel a hamstring stretch — do not round your spine.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to return your torso to upright.
formCues: Keep the movement at the hips with a fixed knee angle.
Maintain a rigid, neutral spine throughout.
Use light weight and prioritize control over load.
commonMistakes: Rounding the back under load (high injury risk).
Bending the knees and turning it into a squat.
Going too heavy too soon.

name: Cable Glute Kickback
instructions: Attach an ankle cuff to a low cable pulley and secure it around one ankle.
Face the machine, hold the frame for support, and hinge slightly forward at the hips with a tall, neutral spine.
Keeping a slight bend in the working knee, drive that leg straight back by squeezing the glute.
Extend until your hip is fully behind you and pause to squeeze at the top.
Return the leg forward under control without letting the weight stack slam, then repeat before switching sides.
formCues: Lead the motion with the glute, not the lower back.
Keep the torso stable and avoid arching to gain range.
Pause and squeeze at full hip extension.
commonMistakes: Swinging the leg with momentum instead of controlled extension.
Arching the lower back to fake a bigger range.
Rotating the hips open rather than driving straight back.
